title: Rotate an array
prompt: Read an array of integers on line 1 and k on line 2. Print the array rotated to the right by k positions (k can be larger than the length), space separated.
starter:
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
k = int(input())
# write your solution here
print(*a)
hint: Rotating by k is the same as rotating by k modulo the length. Slicing the end and the start works.
reference:
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
k = int(input()) % len(a)
print(*(a[-k:] + a[:-k] if k else a))

title: Fix the list reversal
prompt: The program builds a singly linked list from line 1, reverses it in place and prints it. The output is wrong for lists with more than one element. Fix the reversal.
starter:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.v, self.next = v, None

vals = list(map(int, input().split()))
head = None
for v in reversed(vals):
    n = Node(v)
    n.next = head
    head = n

prev, cur = None, head
while cur:
    cur.next = prev
    prev = cur
    cur = cur.next
head = prev

out = []
while head:
    out.append(head.v)
    head = head.next
print(*out)
hint: After you overwrite cur.next you have lost the rest of the list: save it first.
reference:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.v, self.next = v, None

vals = list(map(int, input().split()))
head = None
for v in reversed(vals):
    n = Node(v)
    n.next = head
    head = n

prev, cur = None, head
while cur:
    nxt = cur.next
    cur.next = prev
    prev = cur
    cur = nxt
head = prev

out = []
while head:
    out.append(head.v)
    head = head.next
print(*out)

title: Longest substring without repeats
prompt: Read a string. Print the length of its longest substring with no repeated character.
starter:
s = input()
# write your solution here
print(0)
hint: Keep a window [start, i] with no repeats; when ch repeats inside the window, move start past its last position.
reference:
s = input()
last, start, best = {}, 0, 0
for i, ch in enumerate(s):
    if ch in last and last[ch] >= start:
        start = last[ch] + 1
    last[ch] = i
    best = max(best, i - start + 1)
print(best)

title: Range sum queries
prompt: Line 1 has the array. Line 2 has q. The next q lines each have l r (0-indexed, inclusive). Print the sum of a[l..r] for each query on its own line. Use a prefix-sum array so each query is O(1).
starter:
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
q = int(input())
for _ in range(q):
    l, r = map(int, input().split())
    # answer the query here
    print(0)
hint: pre[i] = sum of the first i values, so a[l..r] = pre[r+1] - pre[l].
reference:
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
pre = [0]
for v in a:
    pre.append(pre[-1] + v)
q = int(input())
for _ in range(q):
    l, r = map(int, input().split())
    print(pre[r + 1] - pre[l])

title: Shortest path by BFS
prompt: Line 1: n and m. Next m lines: an undirected edge u v (nodes are 0..n-1). Last line: source and target. Print the fewest edges on a path from source to target, or -1 if unreachable.
starter:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
for _ in range(m):
    u, v = map(int, input().split())
    adj[u].append(v)
    adj[v].append(u)
s, t = map(int, input().split())
# write your solution here
print(-1)
hint: Breadth-first search visits nodes in order of distance, so the first time you reach the target is the shortest path.
reference:
from collections import deque
n, m = map(int, input().split())
adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
for _ in range(m):
    u, v = map(int, input().split())
    adj[u].append(v)
    adj[v].append(u)
s, t = map(int, input().split())
dist = {s: 0}
q = deque([s])
while q:
    u = q.popleft()
    for w in adj[u]:
        if w not in dist:
            dist[w] = dist[u] + 1
            q.append(w)
print(dist.get(t, -1))
